11|STATISTICAL ANALYSES BY ASTRAZENECA
12|8.1
13|Statistical considerations
14|All personnel involved with the analysis of the study will remain blinded until database lock
15|and protocol violations have been identified and documented.
16|A comprehensive Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP) will be developed prior to first patient
17|randomised and any subsequent amendments will be documented, with final amendments
18|completed prior to unblinding of the data.
19|The results of the key study outcome will be independently validated by an external statistical
20|team.
21|8.2
22|Sample size estimate
23|The primary objective of the study is to determine the superiority of dapagliflozin versus
24|placebo in reducing the incidence of the primary composite endpoint. Assuming a true hazard
25|ratio (HR) of 0.80 between dapagliflozin and placebo, using a one-sided alpha of 2.5%, 844
26|primary endpoint events will provide a statistical power of 90% for the test of the primary
27|composite endpoint. This is based on an overall 1:1 allocation between dapagliflozin and
28|placebo. The study is event-driven. The assumed HR of 0.80 is considered as clinically
29|relevant and has taken into account the HF outcomes in the EMPA-REG trial.
30|With an annual event rate of 11% in the placebo treatment group, 4500 patients are estimated
31|to provide the required number of primary events, based on an anticipated recruitment period
32|of 18 months and an average follow-up period of approximately 24 months. The assumed
33|placebo event rate of 11% is based on a review of recently published clinical studies in the
34|HFrEF population, including the PARADIGM-HF trial. This study is a group sequential
35|design study with one interim analysis using Haybittle-Peto boundary (a one-sided
36|alpha=0.001), leaving a one-sided alpha of 2.496% for the final analysis. In addition, the
37|expected number of patients who will be lost to follow-up is expected to be small; hence,
38|these are not considered in the determination of the sample size.
39|8.3
40|Definitions of analysis sets
41|8.3.1
42|Full analysis set
43|All patients who have been randomised to study treatment will be included in the Full analysis
44|set (FAS) irrespective of their protocol adherence and continued participation in the study.
45|Patients will be analysed according to their randomised IP assignment, irrespective of the
46|treatment actually received. The FAS will be considered the primary analysis set for the
47|primary and secondary variables and for the exploratory efficacy variables.

27|Methods for statistical analyses
28|8.5.1
29|Hypotheses
30|The Type I error rate for the analysis of the primary endpoint will be adjusted for the interim
31|analyses performed by the DMC.
32|For the primary endpoint the following hypothesis will be tested at the 2.496% 1-sided level:
33|H0: HR [dapagliflozin:placebo] ≥1
34|Versus
35|H1: HR [dapagliflozin:placebo] <1
36|8.5.2
37|Closed testing procedure
38|A closed testing procedure including a pre-specified hierarchical ordering of the primary and
39|secondary endpoints will be utilized. The Type I error will be controlled at a one-sided
40|0.02496 level for multiplicity across primary and secondary endpoints and in consideration of
41|planned interim analyses. Statistical significance will be assessed in the pre-specified order of
42|the endpoints as specified in Section 2.1 and 2.2. The testing procedure will continue down
43|the hierarchy if the preceding endpoint is rejected at a one-sided 0.02496 level and will stop if
44|the preceding endpoint is not rejected at a one-sided 0.02496 level. Exploratory endpoints
45|will be tested at a one-sided 0.025 level without adjustment for multiplicity.
